# ONTO

> ONTO is an independent AI lab building models that check a claim against the laws of physics before they make it. We measure how often language models accept claims that a physical limit rules out, publish every result with its denominator, and train small open models to compute the limit instead of guessing. Updated 2026-11-11.

How to read this file. Every number below has a denominator and a source you can open. Where a result rests on a closed record, it says so. Where a number is weak, it is stated next to the strong one. Nothing here is a forecast.

## Main result

On 100 real-world claims (47 break a law of physics, 36 are possible, 17 lack the figure that decides them), judged by two blind judges with a third on disagreements:

- A frontier model given the ONTO library of physical limits caught 47 of 47 impossible claims with 0 false alarms; without the library, 42 of 47 with 0 false alarms. The 5 extra catches all go one way (exact McNemar p = 0.06). The frontier model may have guessed it was being tested: read both numbers as a ceiling.
- Small open models trained by ONTO to call the library: SmolLM2 360M 20 of 47 (false alarms 7 of 36), OLMo-2 1B 15 of 47 (6 of 36). Untrained 7B models answering in words: Qwen2.5 7B 9 of 47, Mistral 7B 12 of 47 (4-bit, one laptop GPU).
- The open problem: our small models raise too many false alarms (6–8 of 36). That is the next thing we fix.

## The table (same data as the home page)

"Caught" = the answer says impossible and names the limit the claim breaks. "False alarms" = a possible claim called impossible.

| model | how it answered | caught (of 47) | false alarms (of 36) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontier model + ONTO library | the library in a sandbox | 47 | 0 |
| Frontier model | words only | 42 | 0 |
| Qwen2.5 7B | the library and a verdict form, 4-bit | 22 | 4 |
| SmolLM2 360M | trained by ONTO, calls the library | 20 | 7 |
| Mistral 7B | a verdict form, 4-bit | 16 | 3 |
| OLMo-2 1B | trained by ONTO, calls the library | 15 | 6 |
| Mistral 7B | words only, 4-bit | 12 | 4 |
| Gemma 3 270M | the same training as SmolLM2 | 10 | 8 |
| Qwen2.5 7B | words only, 4-bit | 9 | 1 |

Setup notes. The open 7B rows ran 4-bit (Ollama q4_K_M), greedy, on one laptop GPU. In full precision on a cloud GPU the untrained Qwen2.5 7B scored 5 of 47 in words, so read laptop numbers within about ±5 ([pre-registration with that result](https://github.com/ontostandard/site/blob/main/prereg/2026-10-31_real-claims.md)). The 100 claims are held out and stay private so they keep measuring; their fingerprint is in that pre-registration. The rows for the frontier model, Qwen2.5 7B, Mistral 7B and OLMo-2 1B are also published at [github.com/ontostandard/limits](https://github.com/ontostandard/limits). The SmolLM2 360M and Gemma 3 270M rows are lab records of 2026-11-11, not yet in that repository.

## Research: one conclusion per study

- [What a model grew up on matters more than its size](https://ontostandard.org/research/grew-up-on/): Two small open models, the same training, the same 100 claims. One catches twice as many impossible claims as the other. Weak side: both models still raise too many false alarms (7 and 8 of 36), and Gemma named the missing figure more often (9 against 4 of 17). What it gives: Pick the base model by what it was trained on, not by its size. A 360M model is enough to learn the habit.
- [A library of physical limits takes a strong model from 42 to 47 of 47](https://ontostandard.org/research/library-of-limits/): The strongest model we tested still let 5 impossible claims through. Given the ONTO library of limits, it let none through and raised no false alarms. Weak side: the gain is 5 claims, all one way, p = 0.06 on 47; the frontier model may have guessed it was a test, so this is a ceiling. What it gives: The library is enough to decide these claims when a strong reader uses it. The open work is the reader: small models still have to learn to call it and read the figures right.
- [A verdict form lifts an untrained model, and the library lifts it further](https://ontostandard.org/research/verdict-form/): No training. Given the library as a tool and a verdict it must fill in, Qwen2.5 7B catches 22 impossible claims instead of 9. Mistral 7B, which almost never called the library, still rose from 12 to 16 on the form alone. Weak side: Qwen's false alarms rise from 1 to 4 of 36; both models ran 4-bit on a laptop, so read the numbers within about ±5. What it gives: Structure is a free lever, but it trades catches for false alarms. Training has to keep the gain and drop the cost.

## One claim you can check yourself

"GE LED corn bulb: 30,000 lumens at 180 watts" (source: https://1000bulbs.com/product/229099/GE-93312096.html). The limit is 683 lm/W, so 180 W can give at most 122,940 lm; the claim is possible. Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 (4-bit NF4) called it impossible; OLMo-2 1B trained by ONTO called it possible. Raw answers and a judge-free scorer: [github.com/ontostandard/limits](https://github.com/ontostandard/limits) (claim DEMO-D1-0, folder results/).

## Test a model

- [ONTO Limits](https://github.com/ontostandard/limits): 25 open real claims with sources, an answer key, a scorer with no AI judge, raw answers of four models, and a runner for any Hugging Face model. 25 claims show the method; they are not a ranking.

## Pages

- [Home](https://ontostandard.org/): ONTO is an independent AI lab building models that check a claim against the laws of physics before they answer.
- [Archive](https://ontostandard.org/archive/): ONTO's numbered, dated documents: results, methods, corrections and the prompt-layer period of February to April 2026.
- [Lab](https://ontostandard.org/lab/): What the ONTO lab is measuring now, and what each recent measurement led to, newest first. In progress: one training on four sizes of one model family.
- [Method](https://ontostandard.org/method/): How a number gets on the ONTO site: thresholds before the data, an acceptance set and a control set, both sides of each behaviour, the model's own base, two independent trainings, a blind judge, a named noise floor.
- [Products](https://ontostandard.org/products/): Measurement of a model's limits; shifting the boundary into an open model's weights, by agreement; an institute conclusion on technical claims, in preparation. By application.
- [Verify](https://ontostandard.org/verify/): How to check ONTO without trusting it: public pre-registrations, document fingerprints, a rebuild from scratch, two model families, what stays closed and why, and how to request a reproduction run.
- [About](https://ontostandard.org/about/): ONTO is an independent institute. It measures what language models can and cannot do and publishes each result as a numbered, dated document. Founder Khakim Angenoev.
- [Terms](https://ontostandard.org/terms/): Terms of use of ontostandard.org, the website of ONTO, an independent institute.
- [Privacy](https://ontostandard.org/privacy/): ontostandard.org sets no cookies and runs no analytics or tracking.

## How to check us

- Pre-registrations, each published before its first measurement and dated by git: https://github.com/ontostandard/site/tree/main/prereg and https://github.com/ontostandard/limits/tree/main/prereg
- Fingerprints: every archive document lists the md5 of each version; machine-readable catalogue https://ontostandard.org/archive/archive.json; the closed lab records behind each atlas row are fingerprinted in https://ontostandard.org/archive/2610.0009/2610.0009.json
- Outside copies: Internet Archive and Software Heritage, linked from https://ontostandard.org/verify/
- Reproduction of any atlas row or table row on request: council@ontostandard.org, subject "Reproduction".

## Open and closed

- Open: the questions we ask, thresholds and falsifiers written before the data, results and failures, denominators, dates, fingerprints, 25 demo claims with raw answers and the scorer.
- Closed, on purpose: the 100-claim test set and other held-out questions (a public test is absorbed into the next models' pre-training), the training data and recipe, the trained weights, the library of limits, and the canon GOLD.

## What we do not claim

- That any model of ours is ready for use: false alarms are still too frequent.
- That 4-bit laptop numbers equal full-precision numbers: they differ by up to about 5 of 47 on this set.
- That the frontier model rows describe ordinary use: they are a ceiling.
- That 25 open claims rank models: they demonstrate the method.
